# AGENTS.md — GitHub Actions

Every workflow runs on GitHub-hosted runners only (`ubuntu-*`, `windows-2025`, `macos-*`); do not add self-hosted, Blacksmith, or large-runner labels. Run Windows steps under native `pwsh` (`shell: pwsh`), keep Mac steps on the default POSIX shell, and keep shared entrypoints as Node scripts.

Pull requests run [`ci.yml`](workflows/ci.yml), which also accepts a manual `workflow_dispatch` to refresh web-session fixtures. Its Linux Node jobs, the Python SDK job, the Linux and Windows x64 Python runtime build (`python-runtime`, reusing [`build-exe-for-python-sdk.yml`](workflows/build-exe-for-python-sdk.yml)), and the native Windows `windows-build` and `windows-native-tests` jobs all feed the `all checks passed` aggregator, which fails when any needed job did not succeed. Master pushes run [`ci-master.yml`](workflows/ci-master.yml), which builds the Python runtime for Linux ARM64 and both macOS architectures; keep master-only checks there, off `pull_request`, so they stay out of PR check panels. [`python-release.yml`](workflows/python-release.yml) builds all five targets for releases.

The merge checks run from three workflows named `Policy`, which run on `pull_request_target` so their definitions come from master, and call the `deepseek-harness-check` action directly: `pr-check-on-head-branch.yml` on pull-request updates gives `Policy / Master Change` and `Policy / Pre-Merge Check`, `pr-check-after-approve.yml` on pull-request updates and submitted or dismissed reviews gives `Policy / Approve Check` and `Policy / Reviewer Evaluate`, and `pr-check-on-base-branch.yml` on master pushes re-runs the head-branch checks as `Policy / Recheck`. Branch rules require those check names, so keep the job names and the workflow name. Each check reads its mode from a repository variable: `MERGE_POLICY_MASTER_DIFF`, `MERGE_POLICY_PRE_MERGE`, `MERGE_POLICY_HEAD_DIFF`, and `MERGE_POLICY_REVIEW`, each `off` (skip), `report` (run without failing the job), or `block` (fail the job); a missing value or an unknown one counts as `report`. `Policy / Pre-Merge Check` merges the commit `Policy / Master Change` reports, so it runs only after that job and stays off while `MERGE_POLICY_MASTER_DIFF` is `off`; a merge it cannot do and a build that fails both follow its own mode, so `report` warns and skips the build while `block` fails the job. `Policy / Pre-Merge Check` runs `scripts/pre-merge-check.ts` under plain Node and knows nothing else about the merged tree: that script checks the released manifests against the root version, installs, and builds the Host and Client contracts, so change it in one pull request together with the build it orchestrates.
